subproblems.title: Smooth nonincreasing cutoff profile with derivative supported in (1, A)
subproblems.statement: Let A ∈ ℝ with A > 1. There is φ : ℝ → ℝ such that: φ is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 φ); φ is nonincreasing (Antitone); 0 ≤ φ(u) ≤ 1 for every u; φ(u) = 1 for every u ≤ 1; φ(u) = 0 for every u ≥ A; φ'(u) ≤ 0 for every u; and φ'(u) ≠ 0 implies 1 < u < A. Here φ' := deriv φ is Mathlib's derivative (0 at points of non-differentiability).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (A : ℝ), 1 < A → ∃ φ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 φ ∧ Antitone φ ∧ (∀ u, 0 ≤ φ u ∧ φ u ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ u, u ≤ 1 → φ u = 1) ∧ (∀ u, A ≤ u → φ u = 0) ∧ (∀ u, deriv φ u ≤ 0) ∧ (∀ u, deriv φ u ≠ 0 → 1 < u ∧ u < A)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 3.3: a C¹ profile with φ ≡ 1 on (−∞, 1], φ ≡ 0 on [1 + ε, ∞) and φ' ≤ 0; here 1 + ε = A). Text: book/chapter-04.txt lines 215–300.
Setting (the Lean statement): A ∈ ℝ with A > 1. Goal: some φ : ℝ → ℝ with, in this order, (P1) ContDiff ℝ 1 φ; (P2) φ antitone; (P3) 0 ≤ φ(u) ≤ 1 for all u; (P4) φ(u) = 1 for u ≤ 1; (P5) φ(u) = 0 for u ≥ A; (P6) deriv φ u ≤ 0 for all u; (P7) deriv φ u ≠ 0 implies 1 < u < A.
Notation: Ψ := Real.smoothTransition; a := A − 1 > 0; φ' := deriv φ.
1. (Facts about Ψ.) Ψ is C^∞, in particular ContDiff ℝ 1 (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff). Ψ is monotone (Real.smoothTransition.monotone). 0 ≤ Ψ ≤ 1 (Real.smoothTransition.nonneg, Real.smoothTransition.le_one). Ψ(x) = 0 for x ≤ 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos) and Ψ(x) = 1 for x ≥ 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le).
2. (Definition and smoothness.) Put φ(u) := Ψ((A − u)/a). The map u ↦ (A − u)/a is affine, hence C^∞ (contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id, then div_const). So φ is C¹ as a composition of C¹ maps (ContDiff.comp).
3. (φ is antitone.) Let u ≤ v. Then A − v ≤ A − u, and dividing by a > 0 preserves the order (div_le_div_of_nonneg_right): (A − v)/a ≤ (A − u)/a. Monotonicity of Ψ gives φ(v) ≤ φ(u).
4. (Bounds.) 0 ≤ φ(u) ≤ 1 for all u, by the bounds of Ψ in step 1.
5. (Plateaus.) If u ≤ 1, then A − u ≥ A − 1 = a, so (A − u)/a ≥ 1 (le_div_iff₀, a > 0) and φ(u) = 1. If u ≥ A, then A − u ≤ 0 and a ≥ 0, so (A − u)/a ≤ 0 (div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg) and φ(u) = 0.
6. (Sign of φ'.) φ is antitone, so deriv φ u ≤ 0 for every u (Antitone.deriv_nonpos). No differentiability hypothesis is needed: at points of non-differentiability deriv φ u = 0.
7. (Where φ' can be nonzero.) Let φ'(u) ≠ 0 and suppose, for a contradiction, that 1 < u < A fails. Then u ≤ 1, or u > 1 and u ≥ A.
   (a) If u ≤ 1, then φ(u) = 1 by step 5, and φ(v) ≤ 1 = φ(u) for every v by step 4. So φ has a local maximum at u (the eventual inequality holds for all v), and IsLocalMax.deriv_eq_zero gives φ'(u) = 0, a contradiction.
   (b) If u ≥ A, then φ(u) = 0 by step 5, and φ(v) ≥ 0 = φ(u) for every v. So φ has a local minimum at u, and IsLocalMin.deriv_eq_zero gives φ'(u) = 0, a contradiction.
   Hence 1 < u < A.
8. By steps 2–7, φ has all seven required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take φ(u) = smoothTransition((A − u)/(A − 1)); it is C¹ by composition with an affine map.
φ is antitone, bounded in [0, 1], equal to 1 on (−∞, 1] and to 0 on [A, ∞), by the corresponding facts for smoothTransition.
deriv φ ≤ 0 everywhere by Antitone.deriv_nonpos.
For u ≤ 1 (resp. u ≥ A), u is a global maximum (resp. minimum) of φ, so deriv φ u = 0; hence deriv φ u ≠ 0 forces 1 < u < A.

subproblems.title: Exponentially weighted ratio comparison on [s, t] (integrating-factor step)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, c, K, s, t ∈ ℝ with c ≥ 0 and 0 < s < t, and let I, I', G, G', J, h : ℝ → ℝ. Assume that for every τ ∈ [s, t]: (D1) I has derivative I'(τ) at τ; (D2) G has derivative G'(τ) at τ; (E) n·I(τ) − τ·I'(τ) + τ·J(τ) = −h(τ); (H) |h(τ)| ≤ c·τ·I(τ); (J) J(τ) ≥ 0; (C1) G'(τ) ≤ J(τ)/τⁿ; (C2) J(τ)/τⁿ ≤ K·G'(τ). Then (a) G(t) − G(s) ≤ e^{ct}t^{−n}I(t) − e^{cs}s^{−n}I(s), and (b) e^{−ct}t^{−n}I(t) − e^{−cs}s^{−n}I(s) ≤ K·(G(t) − G(s)). In Lean, e^{bσ}σ^{−n}I(σ) is written Real.exp (b * σ) / σ ^ n * I σ, and e^{−cσ} is Real.exp (-(c * σ)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (c K s t : ℝ) (I I' G G' J h : ℝ → ℝ), 0 ≤ c → 0 < s → s < t → (∀ τ ∈ Icc s t, HasDerivAt I (I' τ) τ) → (∀ τ ∈ Icc s t, HasDerivAt G (G' τ) τ) → (∀ τ ∈ Icc s t, (n : ℝ) * I τ - τ * I' τ + τ * J τ = -h τ) → (∀ τ ∈ Icc s t, |h τ| ≤ c * τ * I τ) → (∀ τ ∈ Icc s t, 0 ≤ J τ) → (∀ τ ∈ Icc s t, G' τ ≤ J τ / τ ^ n) → (∀ τ ∈ Icc s t, J τ / τ ^ n ≤ K * G' τ) → G t - G s ≤ Real.exp (c * t) / t ^ n * I t - Real.exp (c * s) / s ^ n * I s ∧ Real.exp (-(c * t)) / t ^ n * I t - Real.exp (-(c * s)) / s ^ n * I s ≤ K * (G t - G s)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 8–9 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 3.16: multiply by the integrating factor and integrate over [σ, ρ], here done by comparing derivatives). Text: book/chapter-04.txt lines 382–416.
Setting (hypotheses of the Lean statement, in order): n ∈ ℕ; c, K, s, t ∈ ℝ; I, I', G, G', J, h : ℝ → ℝ; c ≥ 0; 0 < s; s < t; and for every τ ∈ [s, t] (Icc s t): (D1) HasDerivAt I (I' τ) τ; (D2) HasDerivAt G (G' τ) τ; (E) n·I(τ) − τ·I'(τ) + τ·J(τ) = −h(τ); (H) |h(τ)| ≤ c·τ·I(τ); (J) 0 ≤ J(τ); (C1) G'(τ) ≤ J(τ)/τⁿ; (C2) J(τ)/τⁿ ≤ K·G'(τ). Goal: (a) G(t) − G(s) ≤ Φ_c(t) − Φ_c(s) and (b) Φ_{−c}(t) − Φ_{−c}(s) ≤ K·(G(t) − G(s)), with Φ_b as in the notation below (in the Lean goal, Φ_{−c}(σ) is written Real.exp (-(c * σ)) / σ ^ n * I σ).
Notation: for b ∈ ℝ, Φ_b(σ) := e^{bσ}/σⁿ · I(σ) (Lean: Real.exp (b * σ) / σ ^ n * I σ). The hypotheses are used only at points τ ∈ [s, t].
1. (Positivity.) Every τ ∈ [s, t] has τ ≥ s > 0, so τ ≠ 0 and τⁿ > 0.
2. (Derivative of Φ_b.) Fix b ∈ ℝ and τ ∈ [s, t].
   - σ ↦ e^{bσ} has derivative e^{bτ}·b at τ (HasDerivAt.exp applied to (hasDerivAt_id τ).const_mul b).
   - σ ↦ σⁿ has derivative n·τ^{n−1} (hasDerivAt_pow), and τⁿ ≠ 0.
   - The quotient rule (HasDerivAt.div) and the product rule with (D1) show that Φ_b has derivative
     ((e^{bτ}b·τⁿ − e^{bτ}·nτ^{n−1})/(τⁿ)²)·I(τ) + (e^{bτ}/τⁿ)·I'(τ)
     at τ (after Pi.div_apply, the value of the quotient at τ is e^{bτ}/τⁿ).
   - By (E), τ·I'(τ) = n·I(τ) + τ·J(τ) + h(τ), i.e. I'(τ) = (n·I(τ) + τ·J(τ) + h(τ))/τ.
   Substituting, the derivative equals
     Φ_b'(τ) := (e^{bτ}/τⁿ)·(J(τ) + b·I(τ) + h(τ)/τ).
   Check:
   - If n = 0, the n-terms vanish and τ⁰ = 1, so both expressions equal e^{bτ}(b·I + J + h/τ).
   - If n ≥ 1, write τⁿ = τ^{n−1}·τ. Then (e^{bτ}·nτ^{n−1}/τ^{2n})·I = (e^{bτ}/τⁿ)·(n·I/τ), which cancels the term (e^{bτ}/τⁿ)·(n·I/τ) coming from I'(τ). The remaining terms are (e^{bτ}/τⁿ)(b·I + J + h/τ).
   In Lean: rewrite I'(τ), split on n, then field_simp and ring.
3. (Integration lemma.) Let f, f' : ℝ → ℝ. Suppose f has derivative f'(τ) at every τ ∈ [s, t] and f'(τ) ≥ 0 for every τ ∈ [s, t]. Then f(s) ≤ f(t).
   Proof: f is continuous at each point of [s, t], so ContinuousOn f [s, t]. The interior of [s, t] is (s, t) (interior_Icc), and at each point there f has derivative f' within (s, t), which is ≥ 0. By monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc s t), f is monotone on [s, t]. Apply this to s ≤ t.
4. (Sign facts.) For τ ∈ [s, t]:
   - J(τ)/τⁿ ≥ 0, by (J) and τⁿ > 0.
   - By (H) and abs_le, −c·τ·I(τ) ≤ h(τ) ≤ c·τ·I(τ). Dividing by τ > 0 (le_div_iff₀, div_le_iff₀) gives c·I(τ) + h(τ)/τ ≥ 0 and −c·I(τ) + h(τ)/τ ≤ 0.
5. (Part (a).) Let f := Φ_c − G and f'(τ) := Φ_c'(τ) − G'(τ). By step 2 (b = c) and (D2), f has derivative f'(τ) at every τ ∈ [s, t]. For such τ:
   - Φ_c'(τ) = e^{cτ}·(J(τ)/τⁿ) + (e^{cτ}/τⁿ)·(c·I(τ) + h(τ)/τ).
   - The second summand is ≥ 0 by step 4, since e^{cτ}/τⁿ > 0.
   - Since c ≥ 0 and τ > 0, e^{cτ} ≥ 1 (Real.one_le_exp), so e^{cτ}·(J/τⁿ) ≥ J/τⁿ because J/τⁿ ≥ 0.
   - By (C1), J(τ)/τⁿ ≥ G'(τ).
   So f'(τ) ≥ 0. Step 3 gives Φ_c(s) − G(s) ≤ Φ_c(t) − G(t), which rearranges to G(t) − G(s) ≤ Φ_c(t) − Φ_c(s). This is (a).
6. (Part (b).) Let f := K·G − Φ_{−c} and f'(τ) := K·G'(τ) − Φ_{−c}'(τ). By (D2) (HasDerivAt.const_mul) and step 2 (b = −c), f has derivative f'(τ) at every τ ∈ [s, t]. For such τ:
   - Φ_{−c}'(τ) = e^{−cτ}·(J(τ)/τⁿ) + (e^{−cτ}/τⁿ)·(−c·I(τ) + h(τ)/τ).
   - The second summand is ≤ 0 by step 4.
   - Since −c·τ ≤ 0, e^{−cτ} ≤ 1 (Real.exp_le_one_iff), so e^{−cτ}·(J/τⁿ) ≤ J/τⁿ because J/τⁿ ≥ 0.
   - By (C2), J(τ)/τⁿ ≤ K·G'(τ).
   So Φ_{−c}'(τ) ≤ K·G'(τ) and f'(τ) ≥ 0. Step 3 gives K·G(s) − Φ_{−c}(s) ≤ K·G(t) − Φ_{−c}(t), i.e. Φ_{−c}(t) − Φ_{−c}(s) ≤ K·(G(t) − G(s)).
   Since e^{(−c)σ} = Real.exp (−(c·σ)) (neg_mul), this is exactly (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ_b(σ) = e^{bσ}σ^{−n}I(σ) has derivative (e^{bτ}/τⁿ)(J + bI + h/τ) on [s, t], by the quotient and product rules and the identity (E).
A function with a nonnegative derivative at every point of [s, t] satisfies f(s) ≤ f(t) (monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg).
|h| ≤ cτI gives cI + h/τ ≥ 0 and −cI + h/τ ≤ 0; J/τⁿ ≥ 0, e^{cτ} ≥ 1 and e^{−cτ} ≤ 1.
(a): Φ_c' ≥ J/τⁿ ≥ G', so Φ_c − G is nondecreasing.
(b): Φ_{−c}' ≤ J/τⁿ ≤ K G', so K G − Φ_{−c} is nondecreasing; rewrite −c·σ as −(c·σ).

subproblems.title: Bound on the mean-curvature term of a radial cutoff
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P (Euclid P), y ∈ ℝ^P, H : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, φ : ℝ → ℝ and κ, A, τ ∈ ℝ, with τ > 0, φ(u) ≥ 0 for every u, φ(u) = 0 for every u ≥ A, |H(x)| ≤ κ for every x, and x ↦ φ(|x − y|/τ) μ-integrable. Then |∫ φ(|x − y|/τ)·⟨x − y, H(x)⟩ dμ(x)| ≤ A·κ·τ·∫ φ(|x − y|/τ) dμ(x) (Bochner integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (H : Euclid P → Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (κ A τ : ℝ), 0 < τ → (∀ u, 0 ≤ φ u) → (∀ u, A ≤ u → φ u = 0) → (∀ x, ‖H x‖ ≤ κ) → Integrable (fun x => φ (‖x - y‖ / τ)) μ → |∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * inner ℝ (x - y) (H x) ∂μ| ≤ A * κ * τ * ∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 3.16: E₀ is bounded by Λ_ε times the cutoff mass, because φ(r/ρ) = 0 for r ≥ (1 + ε)ρ). Text: book/chapter-04.txt lines 382–416.
Setting (the Lean statement): P ∈ ℕ, a measure μ on Euclid P, y ∈ Euclid P, H : Euclid P → Euclid P, φ : ℝ → ℝ, κ, A, τ ∈ ℝ, with τ > 0, φ(u) ≥ 0 for all u, φ(u) = 0 for u ≥ A, ‖H x‖ ≤ κ for all x, and x ↦ φ(|x − y|/τ) μ-integrable. Goal: |∫φ(|x − y|/τ)·⟨x − y, H(x)⟩dμ| ≤ A·κ·τ·∫φ(|x − y|/τ)dμ.
Notation: r = r(x) := |x − y|. Integrals are Bochner integrals.
1. (κ ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |H(0)| ≤ κ.
2. (Rewrite the right side.) A·κ·τ·∫φ(r/τ)dμ = ∫A·κ·τ·φ(r/τ)dμ (integral_const_mul). On ℝ, |·| = ‖·‖ (Real.norm_eq_abs).
3. (Pointwise bound.) For every x, |φ(r/τ)·⟨x − y, H(x)⟩| ≤ A·κ·τ·φ(r/τ).
   Since φ ≥ 0, the left side equals φ(r/τ)·|⟨x − y, H(x)⟩| (norm_mul, abs_of_nonneg).
   (a) If φ(r/τ) = 0, both sides are 0.
   (b) Otherwise r/τ < A, since r/τ ≥ A would force φ(r/τ) = 0. Multiplying by τ > 0 (div_lt_iff₀) gives r < A·τ, so r ≤ A·τ. By Cauchy–Schwarz (norm_inner_le_norm) and |H(x)| ≤ κ, |⟨x − y, H(x)⟩| ≤ r·|H(x)| ≤ r·κ. Since φ(r/τ) ≥ 0, κ ≥ 0 and r ≤ Aτ,
       φ(r/τ)·|⟨x − y, H(x)⟩| ≤ φ(r/τ)·(r·κ) ≤ φ(r/τ)·(A·τ·κ) = A·κ·τ·φ(r/τ).
4. (Integrate.) x ↦ A·κ·τ·φ(r/τ) is μ-integrable, as a constant multiple of an integrable function (Integrable.const_mul). By norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, with the bound of step 3 holding everywhere and hence μ-a.e.,
   |∫φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H(x)⟩dμ| ≤ ∫A·κ·τ·φ(r/τ)dμ = A·κ·τ·∫φ(r/τ)dμ.
   That lemma needs integrability only of the bound, not of the integrand. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pointwise |φ(r/τ)⟨x − y, H x⟩| ≤ Aκτ φ(r/τ): it is trivial where φ(r/τ) = 0, and elsewhere r < Aτ, so Cauchy–Schwarz and |H| ≤ κ give it.
norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with the integrable bound Aκτ φ(r/τ), then integral_const_mul.

subproblems.title: Comparison of the scale-derivative weights (Simon 3.5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P, φ : ℝ → ℝ, N : ℝ^P → ℝ and A, s, τ ∈ ℝ, with A > 1 and 0 < s ≤ τ. Write φ' := deriv φ, and assume φ'(u) ≤ 0 for every u, φ'(u) ≠ 0 implies 1 < u < A, and N(x) ≥ 0 for every x. Put r(x) := |x − y|, d(x) := −(r(x)/τ²)·φ'(r(x)/τ) and q(x) := N(x)/max(s, r(x))ⁿ. If d·q and d·N are μ-integrable, then (i) ∫ d·N dμ ≥ 0; (ii) ∫ d·q dμ ≤ (∫ d·N dμ)/τⁿ; (iii) (∫ d·N dμ)/τⁿ ≤ Aⁿ·∫ d·q dμ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (N : Euclid P → ℝ) (A s τ : ℝ), 1 < A → 0 < s → s ≤ τ → (∀ u, deriv φ u ≤ 0) → (∀ u, deriv φ u ≠ 0 → 1 < u ∧ u < A) → (∀ x, 0 ≤ N x) → Integrable (fun x => -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * (N x / (max s ‖x - y‖) ^ n)) μ → Integrable (fun x => -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * N x) μ → 0 ≤ ∫ x, -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * N x ∂μ ∧ ∫ x, -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * (N x / (max s ‖x - y‖) ^ n) ∂μ ≤ (∫ x, -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * N x ∂μ) / τ ^ n ∧ (∫ x, -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * N x ∂μ) / τ ^ n ≤ A ^ n * ∫ x, -(‖x - y‖ / τ ^ 2) * deriv φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) * (N x / (max s ‖x - y‖) ^ n) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 3.5: on the support of ∂_ρφ(r/ρ), ρ ≤ r ≤ (1 + ε)ρ, so r^{−n} ≤ ρ^{−n} ≤ (1 + ε)ⁿr^{−n}). Simon prints the factors in the reverse order; the parent proof corrects this. Text: book/chapter-04.txt lines 282–300.
Setting (hypotheses of the Lean statement, in order): A > 1; 0 < s; s ≤ τ; deriv φ u ≤ 0 for all u; deriv φ u ≠ 0 implies 1 < u < A; N(x) ≥ 0 for all x; d·q is μ-integrable; d·N is μ-integrable (d, q as in the notation below). Goals: (i) 0 ≤ ∫d·N dμ; (ii) ∫d·q dμ ≤ (∫d·N dμ)/τⁿ; (iii) (∫d·N dμ)/τⁿ ≤ Aⁿ·∫d·q dμ.
Notation: r = r(x) := |x − y|, d(x) := −(r/τ²)·φ'(r/τ), q(x) := N(x)/max(s, r)ⁿ, D(x) := d(x)·N(x). All integrals are Bochner integrals with respect to μ.
1. (Positivity, (i).) τ ≥ s > 0. For every x, r/τ² ≥ 0 and φ'(r/τ) ≤ 0, so d(x) ≥ 0, and D(x) ≥ 0 because N ≥ 0. Hence ∫D dμ ≥ 0 (integral_nonneg). This is (i).
2. (Pointwise squeeze.) For every x we show (α) d(x)·q(x) ≤ D(x)/τⁿ and (β) D(x)/τⁿ ≤ Aⁿ·d(x)·q(x).
   (a) If φ'(r/τ) = 0, then d(x) = 0, and d·q, D/τⁿ and Aⁿ·d·q all vanish at x.
   (b) If φ'(r/τ) ≠ 0, the hypothesis gives 1 < r/τ < A. Multiplying by τ > 0 (lt_div_iff₀, div_lt_iff₀) gives τ < r < A·τ. Then s ≤ τ < r, so max(s, r) = r, r > 0, and d(x)·q(x) = D(x)/rⁿ.
       (α) 0 < τ ≤ r gives τⁿ ≤ rⁿ (pow_le_pow_left₀). Since D ≥ 0 and τⁿ > 0, D/rⁿ ≤ D/τⁿ (div_le_div_of_nonneg_left).
       (β) 0 ≤ r ≤ A·τ gives rⁿ ≤ (A·τ)ⁿ = Aⁿ·τⁿ (pow_le_pow_left₀, mul_pow). Multiplying by τⁿ·rⁿ > 0, the claim D/τⁿ ≤ Aⁿ·D/rⁿ is equivalent to D·rⁿ ≤ Aⁿ·D·τⁿ (div_le_div_iff₀). This follows from rⁿ ≤ Aⁿτⁿ and D ≥ 0.
3. (Integrate.) D/τⁿ is integrable (hypothesis on D, Integrable.div_const). Aⁿ·d·q is integrable (hypothesis on d·q, Integrable.const_mul). Recall ∫(f/τⁿ) = (∫f)/τⁿ (integral_div) and ∫Aⁿ·f = Aⁿ·∫f (integral_const_mul).
   - integral_mono with (α) gives ∫d·q ≤ ∫D/τⁿ = (∫D)/τⁿ. This is (ii).
   - integral_mono with (β) gives (∫D)/τⁿ = ∫D/τⁿ ≤ ∫Aⁿ·d·q = Aⁿ·∫d·q. This is (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: d = −(r/τ²)φ'(r/τ) ≥ 0, so d·N ≥ 0 and ∫d·N ≥ 0.
Where φ'(r/τ) ≠ 0 we have τ < r < Aτ, hence max(s, r) = r, and r^{−n} ≤ τ^{−n} ≤ Aⁿr^{−n} multiplied by d·N ≥ 0.
Where φ'(r/τ) = 0 all three integrands vanish.
Integrate with integral_mono, integral_div and integral_const_mul.

subproblems.title: Cutoff mass between the masses of two closed balls
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P, φ : ℝ → ℝ and A, τ ∈ ℝ, with τ > 0, 0 ≤ φ(u) ≤ 1 for every u, φ(u) = 1 for every u ≤ 1, φ(u) = 0 for every u ≥ A, and x ↦ φ(|x − y|/τ) μ-integrable. Then, in [0, ∞], μ(B̄_τ(y)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(∫ φ(|x − y|/τ) dμ) ≤ μ(B̄_{Aτ}(y)), where B̄ denotes closed balls.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (A τ : ℝ), 0 < τ → (∀ u, 0 ≤ φ u ∧ φ u ≤ 1) → (∀ u, u ≤ 1 → φ u = 1) → (∀ u, A ≤ u → φ u = 0) → Integrable (fun x => φ (‖x - y‖ / τ)) μ → μ (closedBall y τ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) ∂μ) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / τ) ∂μ) ≤ μ (closedBall y (A * τ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 10 (K1) of the parent proof together with the passage to [0, ∞] of step 12 (Simon Ch. 4, 3.5–3.6: 1_{B_ρ} ≤ φ(r/ρ) ≤ 1_{B_{(1+ε)ρ}}). Text: book/chapter-04.txt lines 282–300. The comparison is done directly in [0, ∞], so finiteness of μ on balls is not needed.
Setting (hypotheses of the Lean statement, in order): τ > 0; 0 ≤ φ(u) ≤ 1 for all u; φ(u) = 1 for u ≤ 1; φ(u) = 0 for u ≥ A; x ↦ φ(|x − y|/τ) is μ-integrable. Goal: μ(B̄_τ(y)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(∫φ(|x − y|/τ)dμ) and ENNReal.ofReal(∫φ(|x − y|/τ)dμ) ≤ μ(B̄_{Aτ}(y)).
Notation: r = r(x) := |x − y| and f(x) := φ(r/τ).
1. (Integral to lower integral.) f is μ-integrable and f ≥ 0, so ENNReal.ofReal(∫f dμ) = ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(f) dμ (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal).
2. (Balls as lower integrals.) Closed balls are measurable (measurableSet_closedBall), so μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = ∫⁻ 1_{B̄_ρ(y)} dμ for ρ = τ and ρ = A·τ (lintegral_indicator_one).
3. (Lower bound.) For every x, 1_{B̄_τ(y)}(x) ≤ ofReal(f(x)).
   - If x ∈ B̄_τ(y), then r ≤ τ, so r/τ ≤ 1 (div_le_one, τ > 0), f(x) = φ(r/τ) = 1 and ofReal(1) = 1.
   - Otherwise the left side is 0.
   By lintegral_mono, μ(B̄_τ(y)) ≤ ∫⁻ofReal(f)dμ = ofReal(∫f dμ).
4. (Upper bound.) For every x, ofReal(f(x)) ≤ 1_{B̄_{Aτ}(y)}(x).
   - If x ∈ B̄_{Aτ}(y), then ofReal(f(x)) ≤ 1 because f(x) ≤ 1.
   - If x ∉ B̄_{Aτ}(y), then r > A·τ, so r/τ ≥ A (le_div_iff₀), f(x) = 0 and ofReal(0) = 0.
   By lintegral_mono, ofReal(∫f dμ) = ∫⁻ofReal(f)dμ ≤ μ(B̄_{Aτ}(y)). ∎
proof_key_steps: ofReal of the integral equals the lower integral of ofReal φ(r/τ), since the integrand is integrable and nonnegative.
Write the two ball measures as lower integrals of indicators.
Pointwise 1_{B̄_τ} ≤ ofReal φ(r/τ) ≤ 1_{B̄_{Aτ}}, from φ = 1 on (−∞, 1], φ ≤ 1 and φ = 0 on [A, ∞); conclude by lintegral_mono.

subproblems.title: Cutoff increment between two annular integrals
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P, φ : ℝ → ℝ, q, F : ℝ^P → ℝ and A, s, t ∈ ℝ, with A > 1 and 0 < s ≤ t. Assume φ is nonincreasing, 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ(u) = 1 for u ≤ 1 and φ(u) = 0 for u ≥ A; q(x) ≥ 0 for every x; F(x) = q(x) whenever |x − y| > s; and x ↦ φ(|x − y|/s)q(x) and x ↦ φ(|x − y|/t)q(x) are μ-integrable. Put Δ := ∫φ(|x − y|/t)q dμ − ∫φ(|x − y|/s)q dμ. Then Δ ≥ 0 and, in [0, ∞], ∫⁻_{B̄_t(y)∖B̄_{As}(y)} ofReal(F) dμ ≤ ofReal(Δ) ≤ ∫⁻_{B̄_{At}(y)∖B̄_s(y)} ofReal(F) dμ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (q F : Euclid P → ℝ) (A s t : ℝ), 1 < A → 0 < s → s ≤ t → Antitone φ → (∀ u, 0 ≤ φ u ∧ φ u ≤ 1) → (∀ u, u ≤ 1 → φ u = 1) → (∀ u, A ≤ u → φ u = 0) → (∀ x, 0 ≤ q x) → (∀ x, s < ‖x - y‖ → F x = q x) → Integrable (fun x => φ (‖x - y‖ / s) * q x) μ → Integrable (fun x => φ (‖x - y‖ / t) * q x) μ → 0 ≤ (∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / t) * q x ∂μ) - ∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / s) * q x ∂μ ∧ (∫⁻ x in closedBall y t \ closedBall y (A * s), ENNReal.ofReal (F x) ∂μ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / t) * q x ∂μ) - ∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / s) * q x ∂μ) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal ((∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / t) * q x ∂μ) - ∫ x, φ (‖x - y‖ / s) * q x ∂μ) ≤ ∫⁻ x in closedBall y (A * t) \ closedBall y s, ENNReal.ofReal (F x) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 10 (K2), (K3) of the parent proof together with the passage to [0, ∞] of step 12 (Simon Ch. 4, 3.5: the integrated expression ∫(φ(r/ρ) − φ(r/σ))r^{−n}|D^⊥r|² dV lies between two annular integrals). Text: book/chapter-04.txt lines 282–300. The comparison is done directly in [0, ∞] for the increment Δ, so integrability of F on the annuli is not needed.
Setting (hypotheses of the Lean statement, in order): A > 1; 0 < s; s ≤ t; φ antitone; 0 ≤ φ(u) ≤ 1 for all u; φ(u) = 1 for u ≤ 1; φ(u) = 0 for u ≥ A; q(x) ≥ 0 for all x; F(x) = q(x) whenever s < |x − y|; x ↦ φ(|x − y|/s)q(x) and x ↦ φ(|x − y|/t)q(x) are μ-integrable. Goals: Δ ≥ 0; ∫⁻_{S₁}ofReal(F)dμ ≤ ofReal(Δ); ofReal(Δ) ≤ ∫⁻_{S₂}ofReal(F)dμ, where Δ := ∫φ(|x − y|/t)q dμ − ∫φ(|x − y|/s)q dμ and S₁, S₂ are as in the notation below.
Notation: r = r(x) := |x − y|; g(x) := (φ(r/t) − φ(r/s))·q(x); S₁ := B̄_t(y)∖B̄_{As}(y); S₂ := B̄_{At}(y)∖B̄_s(y). Both S₁ and S₂ are measurable, as differences of closed balls.
1. (Δ as one integral.) t ≥ s > 0. By integral_sub for the two integrable functions, Δ = ∫(φ(r/t)q − φ(r/s)q)dμ = ∫g dμ. The function g is integrable: it is the difference of the two integrable functions, rewritten pointwise by ring.
2. (g ≥ 0.) Since r ≥ 0 and 0 < s ≤ t, r/t ≤ r/s (div_le_div_of_nonneg_left). φ is antitone, so φ(r/t) ≥ φ(r/s); with q ≥ 0 this gives g ≥ 0. Hence:
   - Δ = ∫g dμ ≥ 0 (integral_nonneg), the first conclusion;
   - ofReal(Δ) = ∫⁻ofReal(g)dμ (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal).
3. (Lower bound, K2.) Let x ∈ S₁, so r ≤ t and r > A·s.
   - r/t ≤ 1, so φ(r/t) = 1.
   - r/s ≥ A (le_div_iff₀, s > 0), so φ(r/s) = 0.
   - A·s > s because A > 1 and s > 0, so r > s and F(x) = q(x).
   Hence g(x) = (1 − 0)·q(x) = F(x), and ofReal(F) = ofReal(g) on S₁. Therefore
   ∫⁻_{S₁}ofReal(F)dμ = ∫⁻_{S₁}ofReal(g)dμ (setLIntegral_congr_fun) ≤ ∫⁻ofReal(g)dμ (setLIntegral_le_lintegral) = ofReal(Δ).
4. (Upper bound, K3.) ∫⁻_{S₂}ofReal(F)dμ = ∫⁻ 1_{S₂}·ofReal(F) dμ (lintegral_indicator). We show ofReal(g(x)) ≤ 1_{S₂}(x)·ofReal(F(x)) for every x.
   (a) r ≤ s: then r/t ≤ 1 (r ≤ s ≤ t) and r/s ≤ 1, so φ(r/t) = φ(r/s) = 1, g(x) = 0, and ofReal(0) = 0 is ≤ the right side.
   (b) r > s and r > A·t: then r/t ≥ A. Also r > A·t ≥ A·s, so r/s ≥ A. Both φ-values are 0 and g(x) = 0.
   (c) s < r ≤ A·t: then x ∈ S₂ and F(x) = q(x). Since φ(r/t) ≤ 1, φ(r/s) ≥ 0 and q(x) ≥ 0, g(x) = (φ(r/t) − φ(r/s))·q(x) ≤ q(x) = F(x). So ofReal(g(x)) ≤ ofReal(F(x)) = 1_{S₂}(x)·ofReal(F(x)) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal).
   By lintegral_mono, ofReal(Δ) = ∫⁻ofReal(g)dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{S₂}ofReal(F)dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Δ = ∫(φ(r/t) − φ(r/s))q, an integrable function that is nonnegative because φ is antitone and r/t ≤ r/s; so Δ ≥ 0 and ofReal Δ = ∫⁻ ofReal g.
On B̄_t∖B̄_{As}: φ(r/t) = 1, φ(r/s) = 0 and F = q, so the set lower integral of ofReal F is at most ∫⁻ ofReal g.
Pointwise ofReal g ≤ 1_{B̄_{At}∖B̄_s} ofReal F: g = 0 for r ≤ s and for r > At, and g ≤ q = F in between; conclude by lintegral_mono.
